[h1] The game is great, it just needs a[i] liiiiiitttle [/i]more time in the oven. [/h1] tl;dr: Game is good. It has some issues with things like netcode and communication but it’s not bad. Very fun game to play with friends. This game is fantastic. I've never played a MOBA game in my life, they've just never been my thing. You'd probably catch me dead before I tried something like League of Legends, Smite, or Pokémon Unite. Despite my dispositions toward the genre, Gekishin Squadra is a game I've been glued to for days, even when I felt I wouldn't play it any longer after a long string of losses I had at the start. It turned into something I'd want to grind hours into; just out of how much fun I'm having playing it. I can look past some of the issues this game has due to how live service games are early in their life, so for all intents and purposes, I believe this is currently a good game. I hope this doesn’t change in the future, but we’ll have to see, given what’s happened to Breakers and Legends recently. For now, this just became my second favorite Dragon Ball game, below Attack of the Saiyans for the Nintendo DS, and above Breakers (they’re both pretty good if you know how to read). I can live without getting the cool costumes, too, and I never planned to spend a dime on this game, so chances are, I’ll never complain about the monetization that goes into it in future seasons, either. Without beating around the bush any longer, I haven't had any issues with the core of the game. It's been consistently balanced, exciting, and well-structured, outside of one or two times when I had to fight against particularly laggy opponents who would seemingly one-shot anyone in our team, or when the opposite team would manage to steal one of the bosses from us despite just showing up when the boss only had a sliver of health and was getting attacked by our entire team, amongst other small gripes. There have been good and bad moments, but none of them have been the fault of the gameplay itself. Despite all this praise, the game as a whole isn't flawless. Outside of those issues I had with the game before that just chalk up to a lack of skill or a lack of decency from other players, the game is still lacking some features most MOBA games have, especially strong communication options and a stronger netcode. There’s also a lot of weird and easy ways to get the game crash, such as running it in fullscreen, playing it without the steam overlay, and pressing P while waiting for a match to start, which is annoying, but avoidable, and not much to go in depth about, unlike the other issues which are much more complex. Most rounds have gone smoothly for me. A problem I’ve had a lot of the time, however, is that it feels like most of my losses have been due to my team not coordinating, and not because we actually had a good challenge. Typically, I play with my boyfriend (They tend to play Bojack, and I just select "Any" on the setup screen and pray for the best) and we both take one of the two routes together, unless I get cued up into Damage with him. We play pretty aggressively and we’re not impressive by any means whatsoever, but I’d like to believe that the both of us do a good job, doing anything we can to get around the enemy team and complete the objective given to us- if a boss enemy spawns? If we know we can let our guard down around the next GOD, we do that. If someone tries to get past us? We gun them down. Usually, since I get cued into Technical or Tank, I don’t get to do as much, but I know we both get the job done, at least. Even when we do well, it seems sometimes our team just won't close the gaps where they need to, even if we’re both guarding opposite sides of the map. Chances are, due to the lack of communication, they believe the same thing about us. That long list of losses I mentioned earlier, for example, comes from this. Frequently, me and my boyfriend would cover one side of the map, and we would be doing well, but suddenly, the entire other side of the map starts to fall apart. Usually, this just is what it is, but no one tries to strategize in this game, and it’s likely because of how lackluster the options are, requiring players to take their attention off the map and try to focus on trying to figure out what details are the closest to what they actually need to get across. The options you have aren’t great either, being locked to players, the GODs, and a handful of generic actions that leave much to be desired. To compare, the start of the round does a great job getting info across -- giving a clear diagram that shows where players plan to go, who they plan to use, etc. -- but communication options mid-round are extremely lacking unless you're voice chatting with your team on a secondary platform, which, along with the lack of information you can get across normally, prompts most people to not say anything to each other during matches. A lot of people have suggested adding Voice Chat to the game, which, while it would fix the problem, would also likely lead to filtering issues and misuse. As much as I want Voice Chat in the game myself, even adding a waypoint system to the game that uses the mouse’s middle click button similar to something like Marvel Rivals, which would change based on context of what the player was hovering over, would help fix the problem, especially since it would show players where they actually need to go, providing more context than what the current system provides. I hope this is fixed next season, because a lot of the losses earlier losses I had felt entirely out of my control, and this will likely continue into the future. That brings me to the netcode… I don’t think I have to go in-depth on this. There’s a lot of problems regarding it. Ragequits not being handled gracefully, confusing crashes and disconnects, issues loading into the game, questionably high ping during gameplay, and lag also not being handled in a way that’s very friendly to players who are polite enough to not play the game at a McDonalds in the middle of nowhere. The netcode isn’t pretty if there’s a considerable disconnect somewhere, and once that disconnect happens, everything falls apart. These issues aren’t frequent enough to make me feel distaste toward the game, but they certainly need to be fixed if the want the game to remain afloat. Can’t wait to see how this game develops over time, and I’m excited for any future content this game holds! I hope the perception of it improves with the fixes that will be made to it. Ultimately, a solid 7/10 game with 10/10 aspects, if you're not insane and believe that a 7 is a bad thing. once you play with more than two people, though, you can never go back. Having more than half of the party in direct contact with you makes you win pretty much every time. Edit: Thank you, Google AI Overview, for telling me Valorant was a MOBA when it's a hero shooter. I hope this cements my point that I've never played a MOBA in my life up until this point.

Has so much potential to be a great game but in every match you que into, your teammates either have a combined IQ of 25 or are simply just bots. Furthermore, every enemy team you play against are a full stack of basement dwelling hob goblins who spend 25 hours a day on their computer. When you decide that you might need to play a stronger character, you gleefully march your way down to the store only to see that the most game breaking characters are locked behind a $10 paywall which forces you to cough up money in order to even have a chance of winning a match. Engaging in a Gekishin Squadra battle is the most infuriating experience in the history of mankind. You could weaken a Majin Bu so much that just farting on him would eliminate him. It would'nt be worth the energy anyways as he will instantly blast of like team rocket, while you take 7 seconds to even take flight and chase after him. Once you decide the chase is a waste of time, you decide to make your way back to your god of destruction only to be met with Perfect Cell and the same Majin Bu that ran earlier, charging up the most diabolical max Gekishin burst mankind has ever witnessed. All the while, your level 5 Goku teammate is watching it unfold as he kills a cell junior for no reason whatsoever. I give this game a 2.5/10 when im losing and a 10/10 when im winning and my teammates are real people.

I like the parts of this game that are about homage and special character dialogues But too many AI matches and the imbalance in character strengths make me hesitant to recommend it to people around me...

The good: -Fun mechanics -Potato PCs can run it -Easy to pick up and play -Short form matches, making for a good daily game to play The bad: -Devs balance characters around vibe instead of logic -Devs introduce items and modifiers that are just not fun and disrupt the flow of the game too much -New characters have the tendency to come out extremely overpowered and break the game's meta for months, and balance patches come very, VERY late -Tons of unusable characters or pointless abilities because of the meta's current state and how little the devs like to buff older characters -Pay to win because of the OP new characters -Ability descriptions are ambiguous, misleading or outright don't include all the details of the characters, nor are there stats whatsoever, leading to crucial information being left out so legit fun characters are not played at all -Card system gets repetitive after a while due to the very few options available, and even fewer meta viable ones (as of the time of writing this review, only 4-5 cards out of the 18 available are meta, the rest are extremely situational or just not as good as the others). Item based builds which are common in other MOBAs could make the gameplay more interesting and make non-meta characters more viable -No real motivation to reach the highest rank as there are no extra rewards for it Overall - Super fun and engaging at first, but once you get the hang of it and start seeing the flaws, the game just gets duller and duller over time. There is legit potential, hope they rescue this game from a meh title to something truly big, but serious work needs to be put for that to happen...

As the game is as of writing of this review. I cannot recommend it. Game breaking bugs which have been in the game since release such as Error Code 0 which can disconnect you during a match and you cannot connect back until the match is over. Which happened during an official tournament to a player, yet it's still not adressed. Character related bugs like Final Form Frieza's rock wall cannot be damaged by most of the characters and has been a "known bug" since he released about 2 months ago. Balancing is terrible. God Goku and SSJ3 Goku have been by far the most opressive characters in the game for over 4 months and they still aren't nerfed. Recent XV2 collab was a cash grab where instead of letting the players just buy the brand new skins with gems like every other skin, you had to pull on the gacha system for the new skins. Said skins needed to be pulled twice to unlock all their effects and the rate to pull them was 0.25% which is terrible for gacha standards. Even in this game, normal cosmetics like Entry animations or finishers are 1% chance to get. Until Toshi and his dev team adress these issues, this game is not worth picking up as a new player.

通行证任务改成什么了，为了日活折磨活跃玩家，不允许玩家一次性把通行证做完？这是我玩过所有有通行证游戏里最折磨玩家的通行证，一个小任务需要2-3把才能完成，升一级通行证需要3-4个小任务才能升一级，一个小任务还分三种不同职业，一晚上就升5级，满级要55级。真就为了日活而日活，原来的通行证就已经是市面上最成功的样式了，每周更新任务，最后一周可以同时完成。 你现在改成便秘式的任务交替，做不完就不更新任务，打两三把把升不了一级，一把差不多要十分钟，真当自己的游戏多热门阿。不说每局匹配的队友跟不开智一样，地图一年了就没更新过一张，每次更新就加个只能收费获取的角色，要不是龙珠ip，你们这游戏就路边一条。 你们这次通行证已经让我这样的休闲玩家失望透顶，平时新角色我都会氪，赛季末玩几天把通行证肝完，这样的游戏体验我已经从第一赛季持续到现在，我相信我这样的玩家是占你玩家多数的，现在你为了日活，整了这么折磨人的改动，让我看到你们这游戏没前途，为了日活不择手段，拜拜了你呢

The developers of this game (Ganbarion of Dragon Ball Fusions glory) clearly have an undeniable love for Dragon Ball as a series. It's evident from the wonderful artstyle, pretty and expressive animations, and quality models that make you forget this game is designed to be rendered in real time on mobile devices. However, that is where my praise for GEKISHIN SQUADRA ends. This game does not respect your time, money, commitment, or emotion, no matter if you're a top ranked no-life or someone looking to screw around with your friends. The team behind Squadra genuinely CONSISTENTLY makes the worst possible choices for its balance, longevity, and good will. In a word, it’s incredible! The gameplay is a lot of fun, and I’m really enjoying it. The only issue I’m having right now is that it sometimes takes a bit too long to find a match. Aside from that, if a player disconnects at the start of a match, the game ends the entire match. The player who disconnected receives a penalty, but the other players who’ve been waiting in line for a long time end up wasting their time even though they didn’t do anything wrong. I have a suggestion regarding this: The penalties for players who leave a match or cause it to be canceled due to a connection issue could be increased slightly. Additionally, the other players who are affected could be given a small compensation reward. Even a symbolic reward, such as 20 or 50 in-game coins, would make the wait time more bearable. I believe that adding such a feature would greatly improve the players’ experience. Thanks to everyone involved!
